items.title: New York Times Stock Plunges More Than 13% as Subscriber Growth Slows
items.summary: The  New York Times  reported higher profit and revenue for the second quarter, but its shares tumbled more than 13% as the company forecast slower subscriber growth in the current quarter.  The company said it added about 280,000 net digital-only subscribers from the prior quarter, its smallest sequential increase in a year.  It reported about 12.8 million in digital-only subscribers at the end of the quarter, and nearly 13.4 million total subscribers.

items.title: Eli Lilly Stock: The One Question in Otherwise Perfect Earnings and What It Means for Shares
items.summary: Eli Lilly  posted a blockbuster second quarter fueled by continued demand for its portfolio of GLP-1 medications, though one glaring question hung over the print.  The world’s biggest drugmaker by market value reported adjusted earnings of $8.38 a share in the period, better than the $6.01 consensus estimate among analysts polled by FactSet.  Revenue surged 48% to nearly $23 billion—Wall Street was looking for $20.7 billion.

items.title: CVS Health Raises Earnings Outlook, but the Stock Is Falling
items.summary: CVS Health  stock was falling Wednesday morning after the healthcare giant raised its full-year guidance on the back of second-quarter earnings that handily beat analysts’ projections.  The 6% decline in share price reversed a 3.9% rise during premarket trading.  While analysts reacted positively to the earnings announcement, company executives spoke in more detail on an investor call about sources of pressure during the quarter—including from a federal drug pricing program called 340B.

items.title: Thomson Reuters Lifts Revenue Guidance After Growth
items.summary: Thomson Reuters bumped up its revenue targets for the year after logging double-digit growth across its three big business segments in the latest quarter.

items.title: Lucid Posts Wider Loss Amid Growing Competition, EV Downturn
items.summary: The EV maker posted a wider loss in its second quarter on charges related to job cuts, as the company continues to struggle with competition and a wider downturn for electric vehicle demand.
